notes: Read in full (307 lines). The 31 CRJ works are taken from the article's own list (ll. 273–303), forenames as given there; only McConnell's page range (133–154) is copied from l.307. Hall, Wharton, Barnstone, Bergk, Finglass, Catullus are cited by name/year only, with no titles. Bernal's *Black Athena* is named without a year. The Sappho-reception witnesses of §5.3.3 (a web page headed 'On Jealousy', a sixth-grade lesson, a poem calling her 'originator of envy', the Attic hydria) are given unnamed and at second hand via #1752, so not entered. Named but not entered as sources read: works named inside McConnell's article (Frazer's *Golden Bough*, Harrison's *Prolegomena*, Nietzsche, Murray's translation, Wilamowitz, Zeitlin quoted p. 4), Sophocles' *Ajax* (as McConnell's topic), the scholars of the historical baseline (Parry and Lord, Burkert and West, Linear B, the Hittite Kumarbi texts), Garfield's citation index (1964) and the impact factor (1975), the IJCT special issue *Future Pasts* and the Classical Reception Studies Network's call (sources the AIO credited, l.226), the 'teaching gallery' of thirteen English versions (l.180), the Gemini 3 default date (l.172, no source given).
